P1.label: Priority 1 — Structural Blockers & Broken Journeys
P1.description: Broken pathways, unreachable pages, blocked assistive controls, or parser errors that actively prevent visitors or search crawlers from using the site.

P2.label: Priority 2 — High-Leverage Craft & Structural Polish
P2.description: Meaningful technical and structural improvements that strengthen image narrative, layout stability, first-paint speed, and canonical clarity while preserving visual design.

P3.label: Priority 3 — Contextual Refinements & Search Enrichment
P3.description: Nuanced metadata, typographic hierarchy, and snippet opportunities where editorial judgment decides whether a change serves the page or whether the current treatment is intentional.

findings.title: Broken internal link returns an HTTP error or unreachable response
findings.whyItMatters: Dead internal links interrupt reader flow across monographs, exhibitions, and essays, and waste crawl budget on non-existent routes.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: If an exhibition or essay has been retired, redirect or link to its archival note rather than dropping the reader onto a generic 404 screen.
findings.concreteRepair: Update the <a href="..."> attribute on the referring page(s) to point to the live canonical destination path, or restore the missing route.
findings.howToVerify: Click the repaired link in a browser or rerun this audit and confirm the target URL appears under Inspected Pages with HTTP 200 and 0 occurrences under Failed Requests.

affectedUrls.evidence: HTTP 404 (Not Found) — Linked from http://127.0.0.1:65515/exhibitions via Read the 2024 Venice Pavilion Monograph

findings.title: Interactive form control lacks a programmatic label association
findings.evidenceType: Heuristic Signal — Verify with Assistive Tech
findings.whyItMatters: Inputs without an associated <label>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby leave screen-reader and voice-control users guessing what information to enter. Placeholder text disappears as soon as typing begins.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: If a minimalist newsletter or search bar omits a visible label above the field by design, either style a visually subtle label or add an explicit aria-label="Subscribe with your email address" while keeping the visual layout intact.
findings.concreteRepair: Add a <label for="field-id"> matching the input id, wrap the control in a <label>, or provide a descriptive aria-label attribute on the control.
findings.howToVerify: Click the label text to confirm it focuses the input, inspect the Accessibility Tree in DevTools to verify the Computed Name is non-empty, and rerun the audit.

affectedUrls.evidence: <input type="email" name="email" placeholder="Your email for salon dispatches"> (relies only on placeholder="Your email for salon dispatches")

findings.title: Malformed JSON-LD structured data block fails JSON parsing
findings.whyItMatters: Search engines silently ignore <script type="application/ld+json"> blocks that contain trailing commas, unescaped quotes, or syntax errors.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Structured data lives invisibly in the HTML head or footer and enriches how exhibitions, organizations, and essays are indexed without changing a single visible pixel.
findings.concreteRepair: Fix the JSON syntax error inside <script type="application/ld+json"> (ensure strict double-quoted keys/strings and remove trailing commas).
findings.howToVerify: Rerun this audit and check the Page Snippet & Schema table to confirm the JSON-LD block parses cleanly and lists its @type.

findings.title: Sitemap XML includes URLs that are disallowed by robots.txt
findings.whyItMatters: Listing a URL in /sitemap.xml asks search engines to index it, while disallowing it in /robots.txt forbids them from crawling it. Search Console flags this contradiction as an indexing error.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Keep private client drafts or internal staging routes excluded in robots.txt and omitted from the public XML sitemap.
findings.concreteRepair: Remove the disallowed URL from /sitemap.xml (if it should stay private), or remove the Disallow rule from /robots.txt (if it is meant to be public).
findings.howToVerify: Rerun the audit and verify the Sitemap & Robots alignment summary reports 0 blocked sitemap URLs.

affectedUrls.evidence: Listed in http://127.0.0.1:65515/sitemap.xml (<loc>http://127.0.0.1:65515/private-drafts</loc>) while blocked by http://127.0.0.1:65515/robots.txt.

findings.title: Multiple distinct pages share an identical <title>
findings.whyItMatters: When several pages use the exact same <title> (for example, leaving the studio name on every subpage without the exhibition or essay name), visitors with multiple open tabs and search engines cannot tell the pages apart.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Lead with the specific work or section name followed by the studio signature: "<title>Exhibitions & Monographs — Atelier Nocturne</title>".
findings.concreteRepair: Give each indexable page a distinct <title> reflecting its specific subject while maintaining a consistent studio suffix.
findings.howToVerify: Rerun the audit and inspect the Search Snippet Preview table to verify every page title is unique.

affectedUrls.evidence: Shares exact <title>Atelier Nocturne — Spatial Monographs</title> across 2 pages (/, /exhibitions).

findings.title: Image elements lack an alt attribute (heuristic signal)
findings.whyItMatters: When an omits the alt attribute entirely, screen readers often read out the raw image file path or hash. Note: An automated check can detect the missing attribute, but only a human editor can judge whether the image conveys curatorial meaning or is purely decorative.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Write alt text in the studio’s own descriptive voice (e.g., describing medium, composition, and light for artwork). If an image is purely atmospheric grain or a decorative divider, set alt="" so assistive technology skips it cleanly.
findings.concreteRepair: Add alt="Concise description of artwork or subject" for meaningful visual content, or alt="" for decorative visual flourishes.
findings.howToVerify: Review the updated alt text in the Design & Editorial Review Studio tab to ensure it reads naturally alongside surrounding prose, then rerun the audit.

findings.title: Images omit explicit width and height attributes (layout shift risk)
findings.whyItMatters: Without intrinsic width and height attributes on elements, the browser cannot reserve the correct aspect-ratio box before the image downloads, causing paragraphs to jump while a visitor is reading.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: HTML width and height attributes establish the natural aspect ratio while your CSS (e.g., width: 100%; height: auto;) continues to control fluid responsive layout.
findings.concreteRepair: Add the intrinsic pixel width="..." and height="..." attributes to each element and ensure CSS sets height: auto.
findings.howToVerify: Rerun the audit to confirm 0 unsized images, and reload the page on a throttled connection to verify text does not jump when plates load.

findings.title: Synchronous <script> in <head> blocks initial HTML parsing and paint
findings.whyItMatters: External scripts in <head> without defer, async, or type="module" force the browser to pause DOM construction and typography rendering until the script is fetched and executed.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Adding defer preserves execution order after the document is parsed, keeping interactive motion or gallery lightboxes intact while letting editorial typography paint immediately.
findings.concreteRepair: Add the defer attribute to <script src="..." defer></script> in <head>, or use type="module".
findings.howToVerify: Inspect the <head> markup and rerun the audit to verify no synchronous render-blocking scripts remain.

findings.title: In-page anchor link (#fragment) targets a non-existent element ID
findings.whyItMatters: Table-of-contents links, footnote jumps, or skip-links pointing to a missing id="#..." fail silently when clicked and fail to move keyboard focus.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Long-form research essays and monographs often rely on footnote and section jumps; keeping target IDs synchronized preserves scholarly usability.
findings.concreteRepair: Ensure the target element on the page carries an id="..." matching the link’s #fragment, or update the link href.
findings.howToVerify: Click the anchor link to verify the viewport and focus move to the target section, then rerun the audit.

affectedUrls.evidence: Jump to Curator Notes (target id="curator-notes" not found in DOM)

findings.title: Root <html> element is missing a valid lang attribute
findings.whyItMatters: Screen readers rely on the root lang attribute (e.g., lang="en" or lang="fr") to load the correct phonetic pronunciation rules, and browsers use it for CSS hyphenation and quote styling.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: If a page mixes languages (such as French exhibition titles inside English essays), set the primary language on <html lang="en"> and mark foreign phrases with <span lang="fr">.
findings.concreteRepair: Add lang="en" (or the appropriate BCP 47 language tag) to the opening <html lang="en"> tag.
findings.howToVerify: Inspect the opening <html> tag in page source and rerun the audit.

affectedUrls.evidence: Opening <html> tag has no lang="..." attribute.

findings.title: Heading outline skips levels or omits a primary <h1> (heuristic signal)
findings.whyItMatters: Screen-reader users frequently navigate long essays and portfolios by jumping through the heading rotor (H1 → H2 → H3). Skipped levels can make it unclear whether a section is a subsection or a sibling topic, though a skip does not automatically constitute a WCAG conformance failure if the structure remains clear.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Expressive design systems often pick <h4> or <h5> for small uppercase kickers or captions because of their default CSS size. Decouple semantic heading rank (<h1>–<h3>) from visual typography by using CSS utility classes (e.g., <h2 class="type-kicker">) so the visual contrast stays identical while the document outline becomes clean.
findings.concreteRepair: Use sequential semantic heading tags (<h1> → <h2> → <h3>) and apply visual font-size/weight through CSS classes rather than heading level numbers.
findings.howToVerify: Inspect the Heading Cadence outline in the Design & Editorial Review Studio to confirm the logical outline matches your visual hierarchy.

affectedUrls.evidence: <h1> "On Light and Architectural Form" followed directly by <h4> "Monograph Essay No. 14 · Autumn Series"

findings.title: Meta description is omitted (contextual refinement — not an urgent defect)
findings.whyItMatters: A <meta name="description"> gives you editorial control over the summary snippet invited in search results. However, an omitted description is never an emergency: search engines automatically synthesize a snippet from visible page prose matching the visitor’s query.
findings.voiceAndIntentNote: Prioritize writing bespoke 120–155 character descriptions for your homepage, flagship exhibitions, and primary research essays. For minimalist colophon, archival index, or utility pages, leaving the description unset or concise is often completely appropriate.
findings.concreteRepair: Where a curated summary adds value, add <meta name="description" content="A concise 1–2 sentence editorial summary in the site’s voice."> to <head>. Otherwise, mark as an Intentional Expressive Choice in the Editorial Review Studio.
findings.howToVerify: Preview the authored description vs. the auto-extracted body prose fallback in the Search Snippet Preview panel.

affectedUrls.evidence: No <meta name="description"> on archival/colophon path (/archive/colophon) — low urgency; body excerpt fallback: "Colophon & Edition Notes Set in Cormorant Garamond and Inter. Printed on 135 gsm Cotton Rag at Imprimerie du Marais. Bound in exposed linen thread so every spread opens flat on the reading table."

editorialStudio.purpose: Automated rules surface markup signals, but preserving an expressive website’s voice and visual intent requires human design and editorial judgment. Use this workspace to inspect snippets, heading cadence, and image descriptions, and record which findings are intentional artistic choices versus repairs to schedule.

reviewPrompts.question: Do the page titles and search snippets reflect the studio’s editorial voice without generic marketing boilerplate?
reviewPrompts.guidance: Check whether pages relying on organic body prose fallback read well in the Snippet Preview table below, and craft custom meta descriptions only where the fallback feels fragmented.

reviewPrompts.question: Where heading levels skip (e.g., H1 to H3), is that a visual scale choice that should be decoupled via CSS classes?
reviewPrompts.guidance: Keep the exact font sizes, tracking, and margins, but map structural section titles to sequential H1 → H2 → H3 tags for screen-reader wayfinding.

reviewPrompts.question: Do photography and exhibition plates carry alt text that conveys composition and subject, while atmospheric textures use alt=""?
reviewPrompts.guidance: Avoid robotic SEO keyword lists in alt attributes; describe the visual work as you would to a colleague over the phone.

reviewPrompts.question: Have custom cursor states, delicate hairlines, and text over photography been checked with keyboard Tab navigation and visual contrast tools?
reviewPrompts.guidance: Static HTML analysis cannot see rendered WebGL/canvas or photographic overlays—verify these directly in the live browser viewport.

unavailableInZeroCredentialCrawl.reason: Static HTTP/HTML inspection does not execute full GPU layout or rasterize CSS blend-modes, background images, or WebGL canvases. Text-over-image contrast and hover/focus visibility must be verified in a rendered viewport.

Heuristics detect missing alt or label attributes, but cannot prove WCAG conformance or evaluate whether alt prose is meaningful, whether custom JS widgets trap keyboard focus, or how VoiceOver/NVDA announces dynamic state changes.
